stem: A team wants their model and column descriptions to show up as actual comments on the warehouse's tables and columns, visible from the warehouse's own catalog tools, not only inside the generated dbt docs site. Which configuration allows dbt to persist column-level descriptions as comments directly in the data warehouse?

option_texts.A: `persist_docs`, set with `relation` and `columns` keys to control what gets written as comments
option_texts.B: `asset-paths`, since it controls what dbt copies into the generated documentation site, columns included
option_texts.C: `persist_docs` only writes to the dbt docs site HTML, never to the warehouse itself
option_texts.D: `meta`, a free-form dictionary that the warehouse automatically renders as column comments

drill_answer_short: persist_docs writes descriptions as relation and column comments in the warehouse
decision_hinge: persist_docs optionally persists resource descriptions as column and relation comments in the database. By default, documentation persistence is disabled.

plausible_options.B: visible from the warehouse's own catalog tools, not only inside the generated dbt docs site

eliminated_by.C: wants their model and column descriptions to show up as actual comments on the warehouse's tables and columns
eliminated_by.D: wants their model and column descriptions to show up as actual comments on the warehouse's tables and columns

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling — asset-paths copies static files for the docs site, it does not write comments into the warehouse
distractor_traps.C: T4: breaks a stated fact — persist_docs is documented to write comments into the database, not only the generated HTML site
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated — the warehouse does not automatically turn a meta dictionary into column comments

stem: A column description references `{{ doc("dim_listings_cleansed__minimum_nights") }}` from `schema.yml`. The team needs to know how that named docs block is actually defined, in the separate `.md` file where its content lives. How is it defined there?

option_texts.A: Using `{% docs dim_listings_cleansed__minimum_nights %} ... {% enddocs %}`, wrapping the markdown content between those two tags
option_texts.B: Using `{% macro doc_block(name) %} ... {% endmacro %}`, treating the docs block like any other reusable macro
option_texts.C: Using a `description:` property directly inside `schema.yml`, with the content needing no separate `.md` file
option_texts.D: Using `{{ doc("dim_listings_cleansed__minimum_nights") }}` itself as both the definition and the reference

drill_answer_short: A docs block is defined with {% docs name %} ... {% enddocs %} in a markdown file
decision_hinge: events.md: {% docs table_events %} This table contains clickstream events from the marketing website. ... {% enddocs %}

plausible_options.B: The team needs to know how that named docs block is actually defined, in the separate `.md` file where its content lives

eliminated_by.C: in the separate `.md` file where its content lives
eliminated_by.D: in the separate `.md` file where its content lives

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling — a docs block uses its own dedicated tag pair, not the generic macro tag pair
distractor_traps.C: T4: breaks a stated fact — the stem says the content lives in a separate .md file, which a bare description: property would not use
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated — doc() references a block from schema.yml; it does not also define the block's content

stem: A team wants to document both sources and models consistently, and also wants to know whether current dbt behavior still treats freshness checking as an exclusively source-only concept. Which TWO statements about documenting sources versus models are correct?

option_texts.A: Both sources and models can have descriptions added via a `description:` property, and both can reference the same `{{ doc(...) }}` block
option_texts.B: In current dbt, freshness can be configured for both sources and models, checked together with the `dbt freshness` command
option_texts.C: Only models can have column-level descriptions right now, current freshness rules aside; sources can only be described at the table level
option_texts.D: Sources cannot use `{{ doc(...) }}` references at all under current freshness rules, since docs blocks are reserved exclusively for models

drill_answer_short: Both resource types support descriptions and doc() blocks; freshness now applies to models too
decision_hinge: dbt provides a way to add descriptions to models, columns, sources, and more. Use the following fields to configure freshness for sources and models unless otherwise noted. Run dbt freshness to check every source and model with freshness configured.

plausible_options.C: wants to know whether current dbt behavior still treats freshness checking as an exclusively source-only concept

eliminated_by.D: wants to document both sources and models consistently

distractor_traps.C: T6: stale behaviour — column-level descriptions for sources were historically more limited, but the documented mechanism now supports descriptions broadly across models, columns, and sources
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated — dbt adds descriptions to sources too, and the doc() function is not restricted to models

stem: A `.md` file opens a docs block with `{% docs dim_listing_cleansed__minimum_nights %}`. The team needs the exact, correctly spelled closing tag dbt expects, since a near-miss won't parse. What's the closing tag?
drill_answer_short: A docs block closes with {% enddocs %}, one word, matching {% docs %}
decision_hinge: {% docs table_events %} This table contains clickstream events from the marketing website. ... {% enddocs %}

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling — Jinja block tags are plausible to misremember with extra spacing, but dbt expects one unbroken word
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated — Jinja block tags do not use a slash-based closing syntax
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated — the closing tag matches the plural docs opening tag, so it is enddocs, not enddoc

plausible_options.B: opens a docs block with `{% docs dim_listing_cleansed__minimum_nights %}`

stem: A column already has a description defined in its upstream model's `schema.yml`. A data analyst wants the exact same wording to appear for that column in a downstream model, without retyping the text and without relying on any automatic inheritance between models. What should they do?

option_texts.A: Reference the same `{{ doc(...) }}` block downstream that the model upstream already points at
option_texts.B: Do nothing; dbt automatically copies a column's description to every downstream model that selects it
option_texts.C: Set `inherit_description: true` on the downstream column to pull the value from its upstream source
option_texts.D: Reference the upstream model's SQL file, which was already compiled, directly from the downstream column's `description:` property

drill_answer_short: Reference the same doc() block again downstream; descriptions are not auto-inherited
decision_hinge: To use a docs block, reference it from your schema.yml file with the doc() function in place of a markdown string.

plausible_options.C: without relying on any automatic inheritance between models

eliminated_by.B: without relying on any automatic inheritance between models

distractor_traps.B: T4: breaks a stated fact — the stem explicitly rules out automatic inheritance, since no such mechanism is documented
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling — dbt defines no inherit_description property, but the idea of an inheritance flag is a natural guess
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated — a description property takes markdown text or a doc() call, not a path to compiled SQL

stem: A source sets `loaded_at_field: date` so freshness checks can find each record's most recent loaded timestamp without relying on adapter metadata. A reviewer needs to know what dbt actually requires of that column, rather than assuming a specific text format. What must be true about it?

option_texts.A: It is a column dbt can query to find that timestamp; it becomes required only when adapter metadata is unavailable
option_texts.B: It must be stored as plain text in strict ISO 8601 format, or the check silently returns no results
option_texts.C: It must be the same adapter timestamp column used as the model's `unique_key`, since freshness and deduplication share one column
option_texts.D: It must be declared in every source's config, even on adapters where that same timestamp metadata is already available automatically

drill_answer_short: loaded_at_field is a column dbt queries for the latest loaded timestamp, required only without adapter metadata
decision_hinge: loaded_at_field: Column dbt queries to determine the most recent loaded timestamp. Required when adapter metadata is unavailable.

eliminated_by.C: A reviewer needs to know what dbt actually requires of that column, rather than assuming a specific text format

D.signal: A reviewer needs to know what dbt actually requires of that column, rather than assuming a specific text format
D.requires_fact: loaded_at_field is Required when adapter metadata is unavailable.

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling — dbt documents this field by its purpose, querying for a timestamp, not by a mandated text format
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated — loaded_at_field has no documented relationship to a model's unique_key
distractor_traps.D: T4: breaks a stated fact — it is explicitly required only when adapter metadata is unavailable

stem: A team drafts an exposure definition and needs to know which single property below is actually REQUIRED by dbt's documented exposure schema, as opposed to optional metadata that merely looks important.

option_texts.A: `owner`, satisfied by either a `name` or an `email` under it
option_texts.C: `url`, a link to the dashboard or report the exposure represents
option_texts.D: `description`, a markdown string explaining the exposure's purpose

drill_answer_short: owner is a required exposure property; maturity, url, and description are optional
decision_hinge: Required: name, a unique exposure name written in snake case; owner, name or email required, additional properties allowed.

eliminated_by.C: which single property below is actually REQUIRED by dbt's documented exposure schema, as opposed to optional metadata
eliminated_by.D: which single property below is actually REQUIRED by dbt's documented exposure schema, as opposed to optional metadata

distractor_traps.B: T8: scope error — maturity indicates confidence level, it is optional documentation metadata, not required
distractor_traps.C: T8: scope error — url is useful context for consumers, but it is not required
distractor_traps.D: T8: scope error — description adds helpful context, but it is not required

plausible_options.B: which single property below is actually REQUIRED by dbt's documented exposure schema
